content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Lansing

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high-school diploma plus five years of experience. Review PMI's full education and experience criteria to confirm you meet the baseline. This step takes 15 minutes and clarifies whether you're ready to proceed.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend instructor-led sessions at times that fit your Lansing work schedule. This PMI-required formal education covers the entire PMBOK Guide and prepares you to apply for the credential.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your training, submit your PMP application directly to PMI, documenting your education and project-management hours. Pay PMI's exam fee at the time of application. Processing typically takes one to two weeks; PMI will confirm your eligibility by email.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice exams and study guides, to reinforce bootcamp content. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. The PMP is a rigorous four-hour assessment; our instructors remain available to clarify challenging topics before test day.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll earn your PMP credential valid for three years. Maintain it by earning Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, project work, volunteering, or community involvement. PMI requires 60 PDUs over the renewal cycle to keep your certification active.
